mainTopic: A personal-altar offering brought into the courtyard, and how פיגול affects מעילה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a statement: once a personal-altar offering enters the courtyard, the courtyard walls 'take hold of it' for every law. רבי אלעזר then asks what happens if such an offering became disqualified and its limbs already went up on the altar: must they come down? The גמרא first infers that he was sure about a regular Temple offering, either like רבה or like רב יוסף. It then rejects that inference, since the personal-altar case could go either way under both views, and the question ends as תיקו. A new topic follows: רב גידל quotes רב that a פיגול sprinkling neither takes קדשי קדשים out of מעילה nor brings קדשים קלים into it. רב פפא challenges אביי with a משנה about the תודה bread, and רבי אבא answers that רב meant פיגול intent at the sprinkling itself. רב אשי then tests this with עולא's rule about a פיגול handful. רבא answers that עולא only meant something on the way to פיגול.

steps.title: The courtyard walls take hold of the offering for every law
steps.stepSummary: Finishes the earlier statement: a personal-altar offering brought into the courtyard is now treated like a Temple offering in every way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The walls of the courtyard have taken hold of it for every matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement from just before this section. Once the offering enters the courtyard, it is treated fully like a Temple offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the מחיצות, the walls of the courtyard, 'absorb' the animal. From that moment on, all the laws of an offering brought in the בית המקדש apply to it, even though it was first set aside for a personal altar.

keyTerms.meaning: They took hold of it / absorbed it
Partitions; here, the walls of the Temple courtyard
For every matter; for all laws

phrases.english: the partitions have taken hold of it for all matters.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the personal-altar offering that was brought into the courtyard. This line finishes the statement just before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a statement that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once a personal-altar offering enters the courtyard, the courtyard walls give it full Temple-offering status in every law.

steps.title: If a disqualified personal-altar offering's limbs went up, must they come down?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks about a personal-altar burnt offering brought into the courtyard and then disqualified: if its limbs already went up on the altar, must they be taken down?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked: a burnt offering meant for a personal altar, which someone brought into the courtyard, and it became disqualified. If its limbs went up on the altar, must they come down?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר asks a real question. A personal-altar עולה was brought into the courtyard and became disqualified, and its limbs are already on the altar. Do we take them down?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally there is a rule that some disqualified items, once they are on the altar, are not taken down. The case here is tricky: the defect, such as being slaughtered in the south, would not have disqualified it on a personal altar. It only counts as a defect because the courtyard walls gave it Temple status.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering meant for a private, personal altar
That became disqualified
They went up (onto the altar)
That they should come down (be removed from the altar)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the question is whether the offering is disqualified. It is. The question is only what to do with limbs that are already on the altar.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asks:
A burnt offering of a personal altar that one brought in, and it became disqualified –
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording that some versions add here.

phrases.english: if they went up, what is the law: should they come down?
phrases.notes: 'They' means the limbs of the animal, already placed on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea that the courtyard walls give the offering Temple status, and asks how far that goes
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the limbs of a disqualified personal-altar burnt offering that entered the courtyard must be removed once they are on the altar.

steps.title: Inference: רבי אלעזר was already sure about a regular Temple offering
steps.stepSummary: Because רבי אלעזר asked only about the personal-altar case, the גמרא concludes the regular Temple case was obvious to him, either like רבה or like רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he asked about this one case only, it follows that the other case was obvious to him, either like רבה or like רב יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא learns something from the way רבי אלעזר asked his question. If he asked only about the personal-altar case, he must have been sure about a regular Temple עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known disagreement about a regular עולה slaughtered in the wrong place whose limbs went up. רבה says they come down and are not offered, and רב יוסף says they stay up and are offered. The גמרא assumes רבי אלעזר had a clear position, one way or the other.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that he asks
It follows that; we can infer
The other one (case)
It is obvious to him

phrases.english: From the fact that he asks about one case,
it follows that the other case is obvious to him,
phrases.notes: 'The other case' is a burnt offering that was meant for the Temple from the start.

phrases.english: either like Rabba or like Rav Yosef.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לַחֲדָא, מִכְּלַל דְּאִידַּךְ פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the narrow way רבי אלעזר framed his question
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר had a settled view on the regular Temple burnt offering case
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that he asked only about the personal-altar case

steps.title: No proof: he asks one question built on another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference. רבי אלעזר may have been unsure about both cases, asking the second question on top of the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asks one question out of another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the inference from the step before. Asking only about the personal-altar case doesn't prove he was sure about the regular case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He could really have two questions, the second built on the first: 'What is the law for a regular עולה? And whatever the answer, does the personal-altar case follow it?' So his second question works whether the law is like רבה or like רב יוסף. That means we cannot tell what he held about the first.

keyTerms.meaning: One out of another; a question built on top of another question

steps.whatToRemember: The inference that רבי אלעזר was sure about the regular Temple case is rejected. He may have been asking two layered questions, so his opinion on the רבה and רב יוסף dispute stays unknown.

phrases.english: He asks one out of the other:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the inference about רבי אלעזר's view, not his question itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A narrowly worded question does not prove certainty about the other case, since it may be a second question layered on an unresolved first one

steps.title: Even רבה might agree the limbs stay up for a personal-altar offering
steps.stepSummary: Even if רבי אלעזר held like רבה in the regular case, he could still be unsure about the personal-altar case. רבה's reason may only apply to an offering that was meant for the courtyard from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה only said 'if they went up, they come down' in a case where the courtyard partition applies properly, since then the partition disqualifies it. Where it does not apply properly, the partition does not disqualify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up its rejection from Step 4. It shows that even someone who holds like רבה could still have a real question about the personal-altar case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה says disqualified limbs must come down. But his ruling may depend on the offering being designated for the courtyard (the מחיצה) in the first place. Only then does a flaw like slaughtering in the south fully disqualify it. A personal-altar offering was never meant for the courtyard, so the flaw may not fully disqualify it, and then the limbs would stay up.

keyTerms.meaning: partition: the boundary of the Temple courtyard
in its proper way: the offering was meant for the courtyard from the start
disqualifies it
he only said this in this case: limits a ruling to its original setting

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבָּה הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabba only said there
phrases.notes: "There" means the regular Temple offering case mentioned in Step 3.

phrases.english: that if they went up, they must come down,
because when the partition applies properly, it disqualifies it;
phrases.notes: He means an offering that was set aside for the courtyard from the start, so a flaw there truly disqualifies it.

phrases.english: when it does not apply properly, it does not disqualify it.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבָּה הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the inference in Step 3 fails: even following רבה, the personal-altar case is still open.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי אלעזר's question shows he followed רבה or רב יוסף in the regular case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The personal-altar case may follow different logic, so it could still be in doubt even for someone who holds like רבה.

steps.title: Or even רב יוסף might agree the limbs come down for a personal-altar offering
steps.stepSummary: The other side of the doubt: even רב יוסף might say the limbs come down here. His ruling may only apply when the courtyard partition properly 'takes in' the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps the opposite is true. רב יוסף said 'if it went up, it does not come down.' But maybe that applies only when the partition applies properly and 'takes in' the offering. When it does not apply properly, the partition does not take it in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposite possibility. The personal-altar case might be stricter, so even רב יוסף would make the limbs come down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף says disqualified limbs stay up. That may be because a courtyard offering is 'absorbed' (קלטה) by the courtyard partition, so the altar keeps it. A personal-altar offering was never meant for the courtyard, so the partition never absorbs it, and the limbs must come down. Since both sides make sense, the question really is open no matter whose view you hold.

keyTerms.meaning: took it in / absorbed it: the courtyard accepts the offering as its own
or perhaps: introduces the other side of a doubt

phrases.english: Or perhaps: even according to Rav Yosef,
who said that if it went up, it does not come down,
that is only when the partition applies properly, so it takes the offering in;
when it does not apply properly, it does not take it in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the doubt raised in Step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי אלעזר's question proves his view in the regular case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Even under רב יוסף the personal-altar case could come out differently, so the question tells us nothing about the regular case.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cannot decide the question about the personal-altar burnt offering, so it is left as תיקו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion with no answer. רבי אלעזר's question about the personal-altar offering stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides from Steps 5 and 6 are reasonable, and no source decides between them. So the question about a disqualified personal-altar burnt offering whose limbs went up is left unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand: the question remains unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's question (must the limbs of a disqualified personal-altar burnt offering come down?) is left as תיקו. It also does not prove which view he held in the regular Temple case.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the doubt laid out in Steps 5 and 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of רבי אלעזר remains unresolved.

steps.title: A פיגול sprinkling does not change מעילה status
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל quotes רב: sprinkling blood with פיגול intent does not take קדשי קדשים out of מעילה. It also does not bring קדשים קלים into מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: a פיגול sprinkling does not take קדשי קדשים out of מעילה, and it does not bring קדשים קלים into מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב gives a rule about what a disqualified (פיגול) sprinkling of blood does to the מעילה status of an offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a proper sprinkling of the blood changes an offering's status. It takes the meat of קדשי קדשים out of מעילה, since the כהנים may now eat it. It also makes the altar portions of קדשים קלים subject to מעילה. רב teaches that a פיגול sprinkling is not a proper sprinkling, so it does neither: the status stays exactly as it was before.

keyTerms.meaning: sprinkling of the offering's blood on the altar
an offering ruined by the intent to eat it after its permitted time
misusing consecrated property for personal benefit, which is forbidden
offerings of the most sacred level
offerings of lesser holiness

steps.confusionAlert: The two halves of the rule work in opposite directions. For קדשי קדשים, a valid sprinkling would end מעילה. For קדשים קלים, a valid sprinkling would start מעילה. A פיגול sprinkling does neither, so nothing changes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next discussion about whether an invalid sprinkling has any legal effect on an offering's status.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
Sprinkling the blood of a piggul offering does not remove it
from the status of misuse, in offerings of the most sacred order,
phrases.notes: A proper sprinkling would let the כהנים eat the meat, so it would no longer count as misuse. A פיגול sprinkling doesn't do that.

phrases.english: and it does not bring them into the status of misuse
in offerings of lesser sanctity.
phrases.notes: Here it is the altar portions that only become subject to מעילה after a proper sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the תיקו closed the previous one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פיגול sprinkling has no effect on מעילה status: קדשי קדשים stay subject to מעילה, and קדשים קלים do not become subject to it.

steps.title: רב פפא challenges אביי with the law of the thanks-offering bread
steps.stepSummary: While אביי is repeating רב's rule, רב פפא quotes a משנה about the תודה and its loaves. Slaughtering with פיגול intent (wrong time) or wrong-place intent still makes the bread holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי sat and taught this rule. רב פפא challenged him from a משנה. If someone slaughters the thanks offering inside the courtyard while its bread is outside the wall, the bread does not become holy. If he slaughtered it before the loaves formed a crust in the oven, the bread does not become holy, even if all of them crusted except one. But if he slaughtered it intending to eat it beyond its time or outside its place, the bread does become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is teaching רב's rule from step 8, and רב פפא starts a challenge by quoting a משנה about the תודה offering and its loaves. This step sets up the challenge; the punchline comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists cases where slaughtering the תודה fails to make its bread holy: the bread is in the wrong place, or it is not finished baking. But slaughtering with פיגול-type intent (beyond its time) or wrong-place intent DOES make the bread holy. So even a 'spoiled' slaughtering still does its job of making things holy.

keyTerms.meaning: The thanks offering, a קדשים קלים offering brought together with forty loaves
Outside the wall, beyond the area where the bread may be eaten
Its surface formed a crust, meaning the bread is baked enough
Made the bread holy, so it now has the status of sacred food
Intent to eat or burn it after its allowed time, which makes it פיגול
Intent to eat or burn it outside its allowed place, which makes it פסול

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of 'outside' here. In the first case the bread is actually sitting outside the wall. In the last case the slaughterer only has a wrong intention about eating outside the proper place.

phrases.aramaic: יְתֵיב אַבָּיֵי וְקָאָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא,
phrases.english: Abaye sat and was saying this teaching,
phrases.notes: This is the rule of רב גידל in the name of רב from the previous step.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa raised an objection to Abaye:
One who slaughters the thanks offering inside,
and its bread is outside the wall —
he did not make the bread holy.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁחָטָהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא קָרְמוּ פָּנֶיהָ בַּתַּנּוּר,
phrases.english: If he slaughtered it before its surface formed a crust in the oven,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ קָרְמוּ כּוּלָּן חוּץ מֵאַחַת מֵהֶן –
phrases.english: and even if all of them formed a crust except one of them —
the bread is not holy.
If he slaughtered it with intent for beyond its time or outside its place —
the bread is holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's rule from step 8 by bringing a משנה about the תודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that פיגול intent does not bring קדשים קלים into מעילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A slaughtering with פיגול intent still makes the תודה bread holy, so a פיגול service still takes effect. It should therefore also bring the offering into מעילה.

steps.title: The conclusion of the challenge, and אביי is silent
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא spells out his point: פיגול does bring the offering into מעילה. אביי cannot answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that פיגול brings it into מעילה! אביי was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא states the conclusion of his challenge: the משנה shows that פיגול does bring קדשים קלים into מעילה. אביי has no answer and stays quiet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a פיגול slaughtering is strong enough to make the bread holy, then the פיגול service 'counts.' It should also count for bringing the offering's parts into מעילה. That directly contradicts רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Evidently, so we see (introduces a conclusion drawn from a source)
Into the status where misusing it is the sin of מעילה
He was silent, meaning he had no answer

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא פִּיגּוּל מַיְיתֵי לַהּ לִידֵי מְעִילָה!
phrases.english: Evidently, פיגול brings it into מעילה!
He was silent.
phrases.notes: It is אביי who has no answer here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא פִּיגּוּל מַיְיתֵי לַהּ לִידֵי מְעִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the משנה quoted in step 9 and aims it at רב's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says the bread becomes holy when the תודה is slaughtered with intent beyond its time, and it does not limit this to a proper sprinkling. That implies that even a פיגול sprinkling brings קדשים קלים into מעילה, against רב.

steps.title: רבי אבא: רב was speaking about sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers that רב's rule is about פיגול intent during the sprinkling of the blood. The משנה is about intent during the slaughtering.
steps.simpleTranslation: When אביי came before רבי אבא, רבי אבא said to him: רב was speaking about the sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings the challenge to רבי אבא, who answers it in one word: 'with sprinkling.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule is about someone who had פיגול intent while sprinkling the blood. Then the whole offering is ruined and never comes into מעילה. In the משנה the bad intent was only during the slaughtering, and the sprinkling itself was done properly. That proper sprinkling is what brings it into מעילה, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood on the altar, the step that completes the offering
Slaughtering, the earlier step that the משנה was talking about

steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule (פיגול does not bring קדשים קלים into מעילה) applies when the פיגול intent was during the זריקה. If the bad intent was only at the שחיטה and the זריקה was proper, the offering does come into מעילה.

phrases.english: When he came before Rabbi Abba,
he said to him: with sprinkling.
phrases.notes: He means that רב was talking about פיגול intent during the sprinkling, while the משנה was talking about the slaughtering.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא אֲמַר לֵיהּ בִּזְרִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 9-10 that אביי could not answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: separating the stage of the service where the פיגול intent happened.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to show that any פיגול intent still lets the offering come into מעילה, against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב speaks of פיגול intent at the זריקה. The משנה speaks of intent at the שחיטה with a proper זריקה afterward, so both are true.

steps.title: רב אשי quotes עולא about a פיגול handful on the altar
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks רבא about עולא's rule: if a handful (קומץ) that is פיגול was brought up onto the מזבח, its פיגול status falls away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רבא: But didn't עולא say that a handful which is פיגול, once it was brought up onto the altar, loses its פיגול status?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי quotes a rule from עולא as the basis of a challenge. This step sets up the challenge, and the next step spells out exactly what the problem is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא calls the handful 'פיגול' even before anything happened at the burning stage. That suggests the wrong intent at the earlier stage, the taking of the handful, was already enough to make it real פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: The fistful of flour a כֹּהֵן removes from a מִנְחָה to burn on the מִזְבֵּחַ
That was brought up onto the altar
Lapsed, fell away (a status that disappears)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rava:
But didn't Ulla say:
A handful that is piggul
phrases.notes: This is the fistful of flour taken from a מנחה. Here it became פיגול through wrong intent.

phrases.english: that was brought up onto the altar –
its piggul status lapsed from it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside source to test רבי אבא's distinction between intent at slaughtering and intent at sprinkling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's answer that intent during slaughtering alone does not create full פיגול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עולא calls the handful real פיגול because of wrong intent at the קמיצה stage alone.

steps.title: Taking the handful is the same as slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי spells out his point: קמיצה in a מנחה matches שחיטה in an animal offering. So intent at slaughtering should also create full פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And removing the handful is the same as slaughtering!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his challenge. Removing the handful does the same job for a מנחה that slaughtering does for an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wrong intent at קמיצה makes the handful full פיגול, then wrong intent at שחיטה should make an animal offering full פיגול too. That contradicts רבי אבא's claim that only intent at the sprinkling counts for full פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: The act of removing the handful of flour from a מִנְחָה
Is the same as
Slaughtering an animal offering

phrases.english: And removing the handful is the same as slaughtering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge by drawing the comparison between the מנחה and animal offerings.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's distinction between slaughtering and sprinkling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קמיצה equals שחיטה. Wrong intent at קמיצה makes full פיגול, so wrong intent at שחיטה should do the same.

steps.title: עולא only meant something that leads toward פיגול
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that עולא did not mean full פיגול. He meant the handful had a forbidden quality that brings it toward פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: עולא meant a prohibited thing that brings it to the status of פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב אשי's challenge by rereading what עולא meant by the word 'פיגול'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wrong intent at the קמיצה only started the process. The handful becomes full פיגול only if there is also wrong intent at the burning of the handful, which matches the sprinkling of an animal's blood. So רבי אבא's distinction still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Something forbidden, a prohibited act or status
Brings to, leads toward

steps.whatToRemember: Wrong intent at the first stage (שחיטה or קמיצה) only starts the path to פיגול. Full פיגול needs wrong intent at the second stage too: sprinkling the blood, or burning the handful.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read עולא's word 'פיגול' as full פיגול here. רבא explains it as 'on the way to פיגול.'

phrases.english: He said to him:
A prohibited thing that brings it to piggul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge from steps 12–13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the cited source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עולא's 'פיגול' meant the handful was already full פיגול from intent at קמיצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: עולא's 'פיגול' means a forbidden status leading toward פיגול. Full פיגול also needs wrong intent at the burning of the handful.
